texts: mixed: everything the sentence says lands (the villagers as a group, the telling, wraith stories, and the time), but the parse never records that Lantern-night is a night — the name carries its own kind word and that typing atom is missing, so the named time is typed nowhere. Split the kind out into its own clause and nothing is lost: "Lantern-night is a night. The villagers tell wraith stories at Lantern-night."
good. the story, its being a favorite, the bad winter and the sixty-three-year gap back from now are all recorded, with the story kept as the subject of "concerns".

mixed: the four wraiths, the rising and "sixty-three years ago" all land, but "in succession" is dropped — the translator has no slot for sequence adverbs, so the record says the four rose without saying they rose one after another. If that ordering matters, spell it out as separate ordered clauses: "Sixty-three years ago a wraith rose. A second wraith rose after the first wraith. A third wraith rose after the second wraith. A fourth wraith rose after the third wraith."

bad: "that winter" has no antecedent inside the sentence, so the parse invents a winter object and files it in the time slot, where only calendar terms and plain time words belong — nothing that reasons about time can read it. Name the time directly instead: "Sixty-three years ago, in winter, three Keepers walked the Cove Stair together every evening." Note also that "three Keepers" here becomes a counted group of the kind keeper, while "the Keepers" in your other rules becomes a single named individual, so the two will not connect.
